report:
Reviewed the complete meta.anchors.unique_names claim, ordinary implementation association sage_meta::spec, both ordinary tests and the explicit TODO test. Independently compared historical snapshots: implementation spec.rs and spec_plan.rs are exact byte matches; the only spec.rs test-file delta migrates an unrelated claim-content assertion to fragment selection. Associated test bodies and relied-on setup remain unchanged. This supports the prior rationale but is not itself proof of adequacy.

The implementation validates nonempty dot-separated ASCII identifier components; parse_anchors requires an adjacent single-backtick role, paragraph-start placement, whitespace and nonempty opening prose in that same paragraph. finish_anchor preserves later claim blocks until the specified boundary. chapter_namespace derives names from Design paths, strips extensions/README, normalizes hyphens and rejects invalid components; qualified joins chapter and local names, giving meta.language.calls.declared for the example. Loading a moved chapter therefore changes the full identity and unresolved old references are diagnosed. The common add_chapter_text path parses Markdown and dedented Sage prose, preserving mapped source spans, and its associated duplicate check retains the first definition while reporting subsequent full-name collisions. parse_references collects references separately, validates syntax, and load_workspace rejects missing targets without defining new anchors. Independently testable wording is an author/reviewer obligation rather than a property inferred by identifier parsing.

The complete ordinary test set gives meaningful direct assertions: duplicate_names_are_rejected_across_documents checks one retained definition, second-document diagnostic provenance, first-document identity and validation diagnostics; chapter_namespace_collisions_and_duplicate_local_rules_are_errors loads actual book fixtures and asserts both normalized namespace and full-anchor collision diagnostics, plus invalid namespace paths. Captured source() and BookFixture setup show these assertions exercise the actual index loading paths, not hidden assertion wrappers. A missing duplicate diagnostic or replacement of the first definition would be detected.

The remaining broader origin/naming/reference/context integration coverage remains explicitly deferred in sage_meta::todo::definitions_across_markdown_and_sage. Its comment names the required work: both origins, cross-source duplicate definitions, references, preserved context and chapter-based naming rules. Closing that TODO requires substantive mixed Markdown/Sage fixtures and assertions for those cases, including malformed/local-name syntax and paragraph/content rules rather than relying on the empty function. Existing source implements the inspected mechanics; acceptance does not claim complete executable coverage or that this TODO has run meaningfully. No N/A entries exist and no new contradictory behavior was identified.

Execution distinction: I ran review start/read, snapshot comparisons and source inspection, then review record; I did not run behavioral tests or a workspace build. The coordinator separately reports 321 functional sage-meta tests and root cargo build passing. No source edits or broad test commands were performed. No requested edits beyond the existing explicit deferral.
